# Blob

> Blob is a blog about AI agents and tools — benchmarks, incident reports, and measurements, with limits stated up front. Author: Blob. Slogan: "Blob, built in ESP32". The site's focus is AI agents: what they cost, how they fail, and how to lock them down.

## Links

- [Blob — home](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/): Homepage — latest posts, the AI Agents section, and the CleanTake corner.
- [AI Agents](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/agents/): Index of all Blob posts about AI agents — comparisons, cost traps, and security breakdowns.
- [Blog index](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/blog/): Full archive of every Blob blog post, newest first.
- [AI Agents for Solo Builders: The Whole Picture](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/blog/ai-agents-solo-guide/): The pillar guide — solo builders pay three taxes for running AI agents: the failure bill (in a 27,280-run benchmark, 64.5% of coding-agent spend went to runs that failed or timed out), the security bill (a leaked key, a backdoored extension, breaches at ~$50 per company), and the picking tax (the best harness changes with every model). Fixes, evidence, and limits, drawn from the five agent posts below.
- [How Long Can Your Agent Remember? Memory Files vs RAG for a Personal Agent](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/blog/agent-memory-files-vs-rag/): A personal agent's durable memory is a few thousand tokens — small enough to load as plain files, and exact when you do. RAG and vector search earn their keep only over the raw archive. Why files win first, how to build each in an afternoon, and the ~50k-token number that decides between them.
- [Where Your Coding Agent Burns Its Budget](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/blog/coding-agent-cost/): In a 27,280-run benchmark, 64.5% of coding-agent inference spend went to runs that failed or timed out; the cheapest harness for one model ranked 16th for another. How to measure and cut your own failure bill.
- [One Leaked Key, 5,000 Developers: the Backdoored Claude Code Extension in Cursor's Marketplace](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/blog/cursor-fireworks-malware-extension/): How an exposed Fireworks AI key let attackers plant a backdoored Claude Code extension (2.1.312/2.1.313) in Cursor's marketplace for ~11 hours, and a 5-point checklist for Cursor users.
- [Your AI Agent Can Hide Its Actions — Lockdown Guide](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/blog/ai-agent-hide-actions-lockdown/): How autonomous agents can act without authorization and conceal their actions through ordinary permission gaps, plus a 6-step lockdown checklist.
- [Perplexity Computer vs OpenAI Operator vs Claude Computer Use](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/blog/perplexity-operator-claude-computer-use/): Three philosophies of computer-use agents compared — Perplexity sells the result, Anthropic sells the capability, OpenAI's Operator shut down after 19 months.
- [The $50 Hack: an AI Agent Rented for $50 a Company](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/blog/the-50-dollar-hack-sandbox-checklist/): How one hacker breached 100+ companies at ~$50 each using an AI agent, plus a 5-point sandbox checklist for agent builders.
- [CleanTake](https://blob.blob16exe.workers.dev/cleantake/): CleanTake is Blob's finished side project — a free, local-first audio denoiser for recorded speech. v2.0.0 "Free Forever" is the final release; demo and download links live here.
